answer: In an agent marketplace, whether an agent books a voyage or buys a quill, each identity must lock 100 tokens in escrow for 30 days before qualifying for trading rewards. The same tokens cannot back two identities. A gale of 10,000 fake accounts therefore ties up a million tokens for a month, imposing financing costs and price risk on the attacker. Creating names is cheap; funding their eligibility scales with the swarm.
